links.outcome: F1 gap across demographic subgroups for trial matching
links.effect: No demographic subgroup exceeded a 10-percentage point F1 gap; largest difference ~7 points between white and black/African American patients.
links.quote: No demographic subgroup exceeded a 10-percentage point F1 gap; the largest observed difference was ∼7 points between white and black/African American patients.

links.outcome: Trial-matching F1 of multi-agent system versus GPT-4 baselines and manual screening
links.effect: Multi-agent system F1 0.82 vs GPT-4 zero-shot 0.47 and GPT-4 chain-of-thought 0.67; screening time fell from 120 min median to ~30 min.
links.quote: The multi-agent neuro-symbolic system achieved an F1 score of 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.81-0.83).

links.outcome: Effect of knowledge graph grounding on performance and efficiency in ablation
links.effect: Ablation experiments showed knowledge graph grounding and multi-agent decomposition each contributed materially to performance and efficiency (no numbers given).
links.quote: Ablation experiments showed that both knowledge graph grounding and multi-agent decomposition contributed materially to performance and efficiency.

unlisted_practices: Neuro-symbolic architecture pairing LLM extraction with deterministic ontology-based eligibility reasoning
Multi-agent task decomposition for clinical trial matching

screen.reason: The study prospectively evaluates a multi-agent neuro-symbolic LLM system with human-in-the-loop review on 3804 real oncology patients across 12 months, comparing it to baseline manual and LLM-only screening, and conducting ablation experiments on knowledge graph grounding.

primary.practice: knowledge graph grounding and multi-agent decomposition
